messages.subject: Survival analysis with deducer
parts:
Hello,

Deducer looks really great and something that I am really interested
in getting my collegues to use. The only additional functionality I
would require for me to stop people using SPSS is survival analysis.
Specifically, Kaplan-Meier and log-rank tests and if at all possible
Cox regression. Would you consider including these? Many thanks for
producing such a marvellous product

Daniel Brewer


--

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: Survival analysis with deducer
parts:
Daniel,

Thanks for trying it out. Survival analysis was definitely on the very long list of things I would like to include. Since it has now been requested, I will bump it up nearer the top of the list. That said, I'm not sure when it will happen. Right now I'm continuing to work on making it very easy to make plug-ins, and after that I may work on a plotting system. If you have some programming skills, you can make your own survival GUI plug-in and share it with everyone. I'm certainly willing to provide support.


Cheers,
Ian

messages.author: 056a0f54645c6009
messages.subject: Deducer query
parts:
Hi Ian,

Quick questions....

I need to go back and read the Deducer instructions/manual, but is it
possible to quickly generate regression numbers?

What I need to do is estimate a set of frequency parameters for bat
calls based on the size of each bat species.
I know that there is a correlation between size the characteristic call
frequencies and the size of the bats.
The lager the bat the lower the Fc is and the reverse smaller bats=
higher Fc.

Based on filed work we have been able to predict what species we were
recording based on the Fc and knowing the sizes of the various species.

Data looks like this as an example:
Species FA(mm) FC (kHz)
SppA 20.5 60
SppB 32 52
SppC 39 42
SppD 28.6 ?
SppE 22.4 ?
SppF 41.3 38.7

Many species still lack verification of matching "faces to voices" and I
am working with a data set from Mexico with many unconfirmed species
acoustically.

What I would like to be able to do is enter the size of the bats using
the forearm (FA) size in mm and the characteristic frequency (Fc) all
known species.

Then enter the FA of those species we do not yet have calls for and have
a regression number estimate for what these Fcs may be.

How can I do this in Deducer easily.

I tired directly in R by my lines of code were not correct and syntax
was really not working.

Thanks for any suggestions.

Bruce

--

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: Deducer query
parts:
Bruce,
You can do this by exporting the predicted values from a simple linear regression.

1. Enter in all your data, with NA in the places where you don't have FC values.
2. go to analysis->linear model, and add FC as the outcome, and FA as a numeric predictor. Click continue
3. In the model builder, add FA to the model. click continue
4. In the model explorer, click Export, and check 'predicted'. This will give you model based estimates of your data. Click run.
5. There should now be a new variable called 'predicted' in your data, which gives the best guess of FC based on FA

Ian

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: Deducer query
parts:
Actually, the way that the code is generated now it only gives predicted values for the observations used in the linear model, so you will need to edit the code a little. in the generated code you will see the line:

tmp<-predict(model.lm)

change it to

tmp<-predict(model.lm,dataset)

where dataset is the name of your data

Ian
